title: kithd: peer_fetch.rs — fetch_peer_blob() implementation
description:
Implement fetch_peer_blob() in crates/kithd/src/peer_fetch.rs.

What: given a peer's mailbox_host and a blob's metadata, fetch the blob bytes from the peer's kithd and cache locally.

Signature:
  pub async fn fetch_peer_blob(
      blob_store: &kith_attach::BlobStore,
      mailbox_host: &str,
      blob_id: &str,
      filename: &str,
      content_type: &str,
      expected_sha256: &str,
      expected_size: u64,
  ) -> Result<(), FetchBlobError>

where FetchBlobError: { HostRejected, Network(String), HttpError(u16), HashMismatch { expected, got }, SizeExceeded, Timeout, BlobStore(io::Error) }

Algorithm:
1. Validate mailbox_host with is_valid_fetch_host(); if invalid → HostRejected
2. Validate blob_id with BlobStore::validate_blob_id(); if invalid → HostRejected
3. Construct URL: https://{mailbox_host}/jmap/download/a-self/{blob_id}/{filename}?accept={content_type}
4. Build TailnetCertVerifier + hyper Client via build_tailnet_https_client()
5. Set timeout: max(30s, expected_size/65536 + 10s) capped at 300s (5 min for 100MB at ~330KB/s)
6. Build GET request with Accept header matching content_type
7. Execute request; on network error → Network; on timeout → Timeout
8. If response status != 200 → HttpError(status)
9. Check Content-Length header: if present and > expected_size → SizeExceeded (do not read body)
10. Read body with Limited::new(resp.into_body(), expected_size as usize + 1)
    — the +1 catches over-sized responses while still collecting exactly expected_size bytes
11. If body exceeds expected_size bytes → SizeExceeded; discard
12. Compute sha256 of received bytes (sha2::Sha256)
13. If sha256 != expected_sha256 → HashMismatch { expected, got }; do NOT cache
14. Write to blob_store with blob_id: blob_store.write_blob(blob_id, &bytes)?
15. Return Ok(())

Defensive programming:
- Never log blob bytes or sha256 at error level (could expose content)
- Do log blob_id + mailbox_host + error type at warn level on failure
- Timeout must be a hard tokio::time::timeout wrapping the entire future (not just connect)
- expected_size must be validated > 0 && <= MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES (100 MiB) before calling
- Return Err (not panic) on all failure paths

Tests — integration (no real network; use httptest or axum::serve with tempdir):
- Oracle: pre-compute sha256 of known test bytes offline (e.g. echo -n 'hello' | sha256sum)
- happy path: mock server returns correct bytes → blob written to tempdir
- hash mismatch: mock server returns different bytes → Err(HashMismatch), no file written
- size exceeded: mock server returns more bytes than expected_size → Err(SizeExceeded)
- connection refused: → Err(Network)
- HTTP 404: → Err(HttpError(404))
- SSRF rejected host: → Err(HostRejected)
